To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the newer colleges and pharmacy schools have fewer faculty members, a higher percentage of faculty members with a doctorate degree, a lower proportion of faculty members who are involved in funded research, a lower proportion that publish in the top 10 pharmacy journals, a lower proportion who publish in the top journals in the field in which they are trained, and a lower proportion who have published at least 5 peer-reviewed articles.

10 of 45 newer colleges and schools of the pharmacy (22%) have a research mission, 11 of the newer colleges and 16 of the older colleges (27% of both groups) have a research focus, and only 3 of the newer colleges have a research focus and a research mission.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential for a "scholarship gap," in which newer colleges and schools of Pharmacy have less of an emphasis on the scholarship of discovery than the older ones.
the impact that the expansion of pharmacy education is having on the research enterprise in colleges and schools.
the impact of the new pharmacy colleges on the research culture of pharmacy education.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the newer colleges and pharmacy schools do not have the same research focus as the older schools and colleges.
the research culture in new schools and colleges of pharmacy is less than that in older schools and colleges of the same size.
the newer colleges and pharmacy schools have a research focus, but it is less than the older schools and that the research focus is not as strong in the newer colleges.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the newer colleges are more likely to be associated with research, though not necessarily with the same emphasis as the older colleges, but are not as likely to be associated directly with academic health centers.
the new pharmacy colleges are not necessarily weaker in research than the older ones.
the newer colleges and the older colleges are not significantly different with respect to the number of publications per faculty member.

the newer colleges and pharmacy schools do not appear to be as focused on research as the pre-2001 colleges and schools.
